correctness.rationale: The parallel-resistor book subgraph proves every edge bound, Rayleigh monotonicity gives the curvature inequality. Simplicial closed neighbourhoods are cliques, and a connected external component attaching at two neighbours strictly reduces a clique-terminal resistance by the Dirichlet principle, proving the complete equality classification. Foster average curvature 1/n then rules out every noncomplete simplicial resistance-regular graph, and every connected chordal graph has a simplicial vertex. Exact spanning-tree enumeration on all 1+4+38+728 connected labelled graphs up to order five, plus sharp extremizers through order seven, corroborates each statement.

originality.rationale: The sharp local triangle-codegree/simplicial Foster-curvature inequality, its if-and-only-if outside-attachment equality classification, and complete-chordal resistance-regular classification are not stated or entailed by the compared primary full texts and public indexed records. value.rationale: The sharp, attained local inequality and its exact equality graph structure give a usable triangle-based obstruction to homogeneous electrical centrality. They imply a complete classification over an infinite natural hereditary graph family, chordal graphs, including two-connected noncomplete instances not excluded by previous cut-vertex restrictions. The exact resistance-curvature separation is mathematically motivated by the new nonregular resistance-regular examples and goes beyond finite recomputation or elementary type checks.
